A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GuideDog research. Their complete main texts, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across renumbering and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original guidance-generation and visual-QA experiments, fine-tuning results, and a 14-participant human evaluation in Tables 3–5.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds evaluator results, human ratings, and original dataset and video-motion analyses.

M1.justification: The four-stage annotation pipeline, S1–S3 standards, object detection and depth components, silver-to-gold verification, and LoRA fine-tuning remain the same. Revised clock-direction wording and additional explanation of relative-depth verification do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds EgoBlind's BLV-recorded videos for an auxiliary comparison with walking-tour footage. GuideDog's 22,084 samples, GuideDogQA's 818 questions, and the principal guidance and QA tasks remain unchanged; new scene and weather statistics characterize existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds Gemini 2.0 Flash to the human-evaluated comparison and introduces a Filtered Silver reference. Gemini already participated in v1's automated benchmarks, whose comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantial evaluation protocols: Gemini-based judging, GPT-4.1 scene categorization with a 30-image human check, and video-motion comparison using 20-second windows at 2 FPS plus manual examination of 50 clips per domain. These supplement the retained zero-/three-shot experiments, QA correctness criterion, 86-image user study, and fine-tuning budget.

E4.justification: New analyses examine annotation rejection reasons and silver-label quality, sensitivity to evaluator choice, scene/weather and regional object distributions, and differences between sighted walking-tour and BLV-recorded footage. Appendix C and Tables 7–10 substantially extend the original analysis of model capabilities.

E5.justification: Table 9 introduces Kolmogorov–Smirnov statistics, p-values, Cliff's d, and effect-size categories for the motion comparison. Appendix D.2 newly discloses single-run model evaluation; this does not establish a change in run counts. Main benchmark results still lack uncertainty intervals.

E6.justification: All original values in Table 3's retained columns, Table 4, and shared Table 5 ratings are unchanged. v2 adds Gemini-Eval scores, including 0.664 for Gemini 2.0 Flash, 0.651 for GPT-4o, and 0.589 for fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL; additional human ratings; and extensive annotation-quality, regional, and motion results in Appendix C.

T1.justification: The mathematical content of the scene and object representations and task definitions is retained. Removing some QA notation does not change the definitions. Neither version develops theorems or proofs, and the added statistical comparisons introduce no theoretical derivation.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the 22K-image GuideDog dataset, 818-question GuideDogQA benchmark, standards-grounded verification pipeline, and evidence of current models' spatial-understanding and guidance limitations. Rewritten contribution statements and additional supporting analyses do not substantively redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning motion-defined hazards, cross-cultural spatial language, and the gap between walking-tour footage and BLV-recorded video, together with explicit deployment qualifications. It also strengthens the interpretation of object-level annotation noise as the principal pipeline bottleneck and interprets regional distributions in terms of mobility and infrastructure.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link, lmms-eval and A100 evaluation details, annotator compensation and student-volunteer information, and clarifies depth verification. Table 6 corrects the listed Roma Walking Tour URL. Existing fine-tuning hyperparameters and evaluation prompts are retained; the PDFs do not establish online resource availability.

R1.justification: Section 5 and Table 1 substantially broaden positioning through Ego4D, ORBIT, ViewQA, WalkVLM, EgoBlind, and research on BLV preferences, cultural variation, and motion blindness. These additions expand discussion of scale, BLV involvement, and applicability. The earlier Zhang and Ochiai citation is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and conclusion receive substantial rewriting, and task descriptions are condensed. The appendix is reorganized into standards references, pipeline details, dataset analyses, experiment details, and AI usage. Dedicated limitations, updated affiliations, and author-year citations further change the document's structure and presentation.

P2.justification: v2 reformats the document, expands Tables 1, 3, and 5, and adds Tables 7–10 and the scene/weather Figure 6. v1's geographic Figures 4–5 become a combined Figure 4. Prompt panels and examples are resized or relocated, with two formerly separate appendix examples sharing a page.

improvement.justification: The new dataset audits, comparison with BLV-recorded footage, broader research context, and explicit limitations improve transparency and assessment of validity. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Table 3 does not support the claimed consistent evaluator rankings, and Appendix C.3's 332-video sample per domain is not reconciled with the 269 source videos reported in Table 2.
